description_en: Cyāsal is home to almost 20phalcā, but Nārāṃhiṭī Phalcā is the largest of them all. Its L-shaped building was previously made up of two separatephalcā(one facing west, the other south). These were constructed at different times, and later united during the restoration of the site in 2018. According to the head of the Phalcā Renovation Committee, the smallerphalcā (which opens up to the south) had two bays, whilst the longer one (facing west) had eight. At the centre of the longerphalcā,there was once a passage to go down to thehiṭī. These steps were later removed during its renovation in the 1990s. Thephalcāborders Nārāṃhiṭi or Nāyahiṭi at the west and, partly, the south-west, and is attached to the building that houses the Gajalakṣmī Khānepānī Vyavasthāpan Samiti (English: "Gajalakṣmī Drinking Water Management Committee") at the east. The western wing is dedicated to Bhimsen and an inscription dated 1750 CE documents its origin. Its ritual meaning is also related to a statue of of Gajalakṣmī. Dating back to 200 BC, this statue is one of the oldest in the Kathmandu Valley, and is positioned at the bottom of thehiti,next to the spring. Thephalcācollapsed in the 2015 earthquake and was replaced with a provisional structure, so as to allowbhajananddāpha bhajanto be performed. Only a few historical fragments were used in its replacement, which was funded by Photo Kathmandu (2015 and 2016 edition), UNESCO and the Kwelachhi Tol Sudhar Samiti¨, Ward No 9/11.Before the earthquake, the largerphalcāwas called Bhaila Capaḥ of Nhesaḥ Kumhā/Avāḥ.Tiwari(1994) refers to it as Nayo Hiti (inventory number 14.1a). The smallerphalcāwas looked after and used by theguthiof the Āśālāl Avāle. Tiwari also refers to it as Nayo Hiti Jadhu (inv. no 34.2b) and reports that there were plans to establish a garden in front of thephalcāin order to prevent garbage dumping and parking (1994:7).S.R.Tiwari's (1994:34) description of thephalcā(he writes 'falca') reads:"Its original shape is much changed. It appears that the falca was actually in two complementary parts situated on either side of the approach steps to the pit conduit and had a continuous roof over it. This can be concluded from the structure under the plinth of the falca. It appears to have changed to its current shape in late Rana period. The falca now also has an added on look with the extention to the south side. The unit to the north has six bays and the southern unit is L-shaped with five (3+2) bays. The roof is of jhingati tiles and is a hipped gable. The two roofs do not join properly. Both the component falcas are in very advanced state of decay. the one to the south being in worse condition. Characteristic window formations on the back wall is noted". Tiwari also includes a photograph of thephalchāfrom the early 1990s in report on page 37.Speaking to those concerned with architectural conservation (or a conservation action plan), Tiwari recommends the following in his 1994 report of Cyasa:"Nayo Hiti and Capa ensemble ( 31.2a, 14.la, etc.): Activation of the stone water conduits and clearing of its two reported sources and control of pollution entry locations from the first 'manhole' within settled area, improvement of drainage of pit, repaving ofhiti floor, action of the twin falcas to the west incorporating two basement rooms on either side of the main approach stairway, reconstruction of the corner falca as 'sunning unit', redesign and replacement of the way side seating to the north, relocation of the inscription and sculpture ( 56.6b, 60.6c) in dry positions, closure of east steps to first platform, relocation of 'Buddha image', clearance of encroachment in front upto Awah Guthi Capa, etc." (p. 24). Apparently, a statue of Buddha had been placed there in the early 1990s as a move towards 'beautification'.After the earthquakes of 2015, Nārāṃhiṭī Phalcā was very badly damaged and had to be demolished down to its plinth. The analysis of the collapse was undertaken in the name of photo.circle, which raised 12,000 US dollars for the reconstruction from donations made to PhotoKathmandu 2015. These funds also came from their limited edition print sale of archival photographs from the Nepal Picture Library and the Peace Corps Nepal Photo History Project. A third collection of contemporary photographs was donated by friends of photo.circle. It was discovered that there were been an insufficient number of roof-supporting rafters, a lack of seismic strengthening features (e.g. plywood diaphragms in roof planes, diagonal bracing) and insufficient anchoring of the columns to the platform in the stone platform. Since the platform was still in good shape, there was no need for it to be renovated. However, the remaining 1m-high back wall was dismantled, as was the small part of the 'L' that was still standing but damaged. These were rebuilt with the use of as much of the old material as was possible. 16 plain columns were found but most were in bad quality; they were found to be too small to support the roof. 6 of the carved columns were salvaged and were in good conditon. The project proposal therefore planned for them to be reused (dating from the 'original' pati from before that previous reconstruction). 10 carved columns were to be made new, but were based on the design of the salvaged ones. Similarly, the project foresaw the construction of 19 new capitals to be made (no capitals were used in the last restoration phase, which did not prepare the structre well for earthquakes). The walls, windows and roof structure were also to be reconstructed from all new materials, including a corrugated roof. Altogether, the project was estimated to require around 35,500 US dollars (from the project proposal, p. 3-4).PhotoKathmandu 2015 dedicated much attention to thephalcā.They exhibited some historical photographs from the neighbourhood there and elsewhere around Cyāsal.
description_ne: च्यासल चोकको दक्षिणपट्टि क्वय्लाछिमा यो फल्चा रहेको छ । ९ वटा कवल भएको लामो र अन्य कुनै संरचनासँग नजोडिएको यो फल्चा पश्चिमतर्फ फर्किएको छ र यसको पछाडि नारायण हिटी नामक धारो र गजलक्ष्मीको मूर्ति रहेको छ । नेउत कुतिसौगः चौबाटोबाट च्यासल जाने खपिंछेँको गल्लीमा यो फल्चा रहेको छ । यसै फल्चाको जसलाई चीधं फल्चा पनि भनिन्छ, गजलक्ष्मी खाने पानी व्यवस्थापन समितिको भवनसँग जोडिएको छ । पहिला यस ठाउँमा दुई वटा अलग अलग फल्चा थिए, जसलाई पछि जोडियो र एल् आकारको एउटै फल्चा बनाइयो । त्यस कारण एउटै फल्चा भए पनि आजभोलि यसका दुईवटा नाम "लामो फल्चा" र "छोटो फल्चा" प्रसिद्ध छन् । सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पमा यो फल्चा पूरै ध्वस्त भएको थियो र भर्खरै सन् २०१८ मा यसको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको छ ।
monument_assessment: Collapsed, Rebuilt, Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)

historical_events.event_name: Construction of the southern Phalcā and donation of land
historical_events.event_description: The inscription in the southern Phalcā mentions its construction and the offering of "two ropanis of land called Yantābu" for the building.

The inscription in the western wing states that a group of Prajāpatis/Avāles led by Kṛṣṇamuni Bare (śākya) initiated the construction of a six-bayedPhalcā devoted to Bhīmarāṇeśvara and established a statue of Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara (inside the Phalcā). From here, Rām Prajāpati and his family were appointed as the caretakers of thePhalcā. The inscription also mentions the offering of wick lamps, rice and meat on the festivals of Buṃgama Lokeśvara and Indrajātra.

Reconstruction of the Phalcā was carried out by GTZ/udle. Reportedly, there was a marble inscription documenting this event, but today (effective 2019) it is lost. Presumably this happened during the earthquake and the subsequent reconstruction.

Reconstruction of the Phalcā after its collapse folowing the 2015 earthquakes. The reconstruction was financed by photo.circle Kathmandu, UNESCO and local people. Thedhuri pūjāof Nāraṃhiṭi Phalcā was performed by Sānukāji Avāle (52), Kvaylāchi on 9 June 2018. Photo.circle has shared a report about the reconstruction with the NHDP. Photo.circle contributed 12,000 US dollars to the restoration project. Most of these donations came from the PhotoKathmandu festival and UNESCO.
